thread:
Anya: Heads-up — nightly perf job (gptx, seq=4096, batch=8) hit an OOM even though GPU free memory looked sane. Quick dump attached below.

Matt: Can you paste the profiler snippet / which kernel chooser picked?

Anya: Paste of the key lines:
```
kernel_choice: flash_attention_v2 (seq=4096, b=8) -> workspace=1.9G
ffn: cublaslt_gemm_f32 -> temp_workspace=2.4G
kv_cache_current_size=3.1G
slab_reserved=5.0G
OOM at allocator::alloc_temp (requested 512MB)
```

Leo: That workspace delta is ugly — FA choosing for attn vs Triton fallback often changes temp pattern. For seq 4096 FlashAttention wants large contiguous workspace which spikes slab fragmentation.

Sanjay: Did we re-enable slot reservation last week? I vaguely remember a change that pre-reserved worst-case chunk for each op which increases peak.

Anya: We rolled "micro-slotting" on canary. The intention was to avoid tiny alloc churn but it may be over-reserving contiguous ranges.

InfraBot: CI/Perf-job #8765 finished with status: failed (OOM) :warning:

Rachel: Quick experiments to triage: 1) force Triton attn fallback to see memory profile, 2) run with KV eviction threshold lowered (free earlier), 3) enable transient buffer reuse across FFN steps.

Matt: For transient reuse: currently allocator hands out per-layer temp buffers and they free immediately after each op. But we still leave pinned slab fragments because of contiguous workspace alignment. If we add a reuse ring for same-size temps we can reduce fragmentation and peak by ~20-30% (from local tests).

Leo: Also we should log kernel name + workspace usage at op-level in traces (low overhead sampling). That helps correlate chooser decisions with OOMs.

Sanjay: Suggestion: implement a soft headroom check in kernel chooser — prefer kernel with lower workspace if (kv_cache_size + expected_workspace) > (slab_free * 0.75). This biases away from FA when cache pressure is high.

Anya: I ran forced-triton_attn run: results below
```
kernel_choice: triton_attention (seq=4096, b=8) -> workspace=600MB
ffn: cublaslt_gemm_f32 -> temp_workspace=2.1G
kv_cache_current_size=3.0G
slab_reserved=4.2G
peak_mem=11.3G (no OOM)
```
So switching attention kernel avoids the OOM on nightly. FFN temp still big but under threshold.

Rachel: Good signal. That means kernel chooser needs a workspace-aware cost function (not just latency). We can add a cost = latency + alpha * (workspace_bytes / slab_total). Tune alpha conservatively.

Matt: I'll prototype allocator slot reuse + a small freelist for the typical FFN temp sizes (64MB, 128MB, 256MB) to cut repeated mallocs and fragmentation.

Sanjay: I'll add a low-overhead tracer counter: op -> (chosen_kernel, workspace_bytes, slab_free_before). Sample 1/10 requests initially.

Leo: Ops for rollout: 1) add chooser soft-headroom heuristic, 2) add op-level workspace traces, 3) implement transient temp freelist, 4) lower KV eviction trigger under memory pressure. Plan to canary to dedicated env and measure regressions.

Anya: Timeline: I'll run a couple more forced-fallback experiments today and post exact peak numbers. If results match, we can ship chooser change as an opt-in runtime flag first.

Rachel: Sounds good. Matt/Sanjay — coordinate PRs. I'll own the telemetry dashboard change to surface workspace per-op. :thumbsup:

Matt: Pinged you on PR draft, will add unit tests for freelist behavior.

Anya: Thanks all — will update with numeric diffs once I finish the runs.
